steps.raw_response:
Perspective: Carolyn Abebe

From where I stand, after Scenario 3 I felt hopeful. Marilyn had accepted my invitation warmly, and I believed we were building something genuine beyond just being coworkers. My intention then was to keep nurturing that friendship, to be someone she could trust and lean on, and to offer her connection outside the stress of the bank.

By Scenario 4, something shifted. Even though we had those friendly moments outside work, I noticed she still kept me at arm’s length during our shifts. That confused me and stung a little. I had opened up, I had invited her in, and I thought we had turned a corner—but at the bank it felt like a wall remained. So my intention changed. I no longer just wanted to strengthen the friendship; I wanted to understand why the distance was there and address it directly. I wanted to confront the professional gap between us, not out of anger, but because I cared about our working relationship and wanted it to feel as real and connected as the personal one seemed to be becoming.

So yes, my intention shifted from wanting to strengthen the friendship and offer support to wanting to confront the professional distance and improve our work dynamic.
